facts: Built-in CPU capture uses perf on Linux and DTrace on macOS. Remote capture host is Linux; WSL requires WSL2/perf.
Import/export on other platforms is not native Windows collection. CPU stacks/time are not heap leak attribution.
Valgrind integration supports Linux/macOS and Windows using WSL. A WSL toolchain/profile builds a Linux target. Native Windows PE executables are not covered by that statement.
CLion integrates sanitizer output, but compiler/platform support determines availability. Windows recipe documents clang-cl under MSVC; instrumentation requires a rebuild.
The generic detect_leaks option must not be interpreted as Windows LSan support.
MSVC supports /fsanitize=address on Windowsx86/x64. It diagnoses classes of invalid accesses, mismatched frees, overflows and use-after-free.
MSVC documentation lists leak/thread/memory sanitizers as unsupported future directions; clean ASan output is not a leak-free certificate.
Disable /RTC, incremental linking and Edit-and-Continue for ASan. Partially instrumented modules reduce coverage.
ASan retains memory during execution and reserves shadow address space, so OS process growth during ASan runs is not directly comparable to a normal build.
Debug CRT offers _CrtDumpMemoryLeaks and scoped _CrtMemCheckpoint/_CrtMemDifference. Debug heap records standard CRT allocation paths; Release uses ordinary malloc/free.
Reports can include library allocations whose destructors have not yet run. Scope and teardown timing matter; GPU allocations and arbitrary custom heaps are not universally covered.
Supported platforms include Linux; Windows is absent. LSan checks for unreachable leaks near process exit, standalone or with ASan.
-fsanitize=address instruments invalid accesses; -fsanitize=leak links allocation interception; -fsanitize=undefined checks selected undefined behavior. Runtime options control diagnostics.
PrivateMemorySize64 reports process memory not shareable with other processes and corresponds to Private Bytes. Refresh the Process object before sampling.
WorkingSet64 is resident physical memory, including shared and private pages. It is not the amount of live heap allocations.
CLion status-bar memory indicator and -Xmx concern the IDE JVM heap, not the engine process.
Debugger Memory View displays bytes at selected addresses and highlights changes. It does not enumerate ownership leaks.
